pearl: ST elevation in two contiguous leads means reperfusion now: PCI within 90 minutes, or lytics within 30 if PCI is more than 120 minutes away. Troponin confirms but never delays.
buzz: Inferior MI (II, III, aVF) - get right-sided leads. RV infarct is preload-dependent, so nitrates can cause profound hypotension.

pearl: Rate control with a beta blocker or diltiazem unless unstable, then synchronized cardioversion. Anticoagulate by CHA2DS2-VASc, independent of whether you chose rate or rhythm control.
buzz: AF over 48 hours without anticoagulation - TEE first, or 3 weeks of anticoagulation before cardioversion.

pearl: Four drug classes lower mortality: ACEi or ARNI, beta blocker, mineralocorticoid antagonist, SGLT2 inhibitor. Loop diuretics relieve symptoms but do not extend life.
buzz: Do not start a beta blocker during acute decompensation. Add it once the patient is euvolemic.

pearl: Once severe AS causes syncope, angina, or dyspnea, valve replacement is the only thing that changes the trajectory. Medical therapy does not.
buzz: Late-peaking crescendo-decrescendo murmur with a delayed carotid upstroke (pulsus parvus et tardus).

pearl: Three sets of blood cultures from separate sites before antibiotics, then echocardiography. Modified Duke criteria formalize the diagnosis.
buzz: Streptococcus gallolyticus (bovis) bacteremia - colonoscopy to look for colorectal cancer.

pearl: Wells score first. Low probability means D-dimer can exclude it. Moderate or high probability goes straight to compression ultrasound - a negative D-dimer will not save you there.
buzz: Provoked by surgery: 3 months of anticoagulation. Unprovoked: at least 3 months, then reassess for indefinite therapy.

pearl: Hemodynamically unstable means thrombolysis. Stable means anticoagulation. CTA is the test unless renal failure or pregnancy, where V/Q scanning wins.
buzz: In pregnancy, start with bilateral leg ultrasound - a positive result lets you treat without imaging the chest.

pearl: Type A involving the ascending aorta is a surgical emergency. Type B is medical: IV beta blocker BEFORE any vasodilator, or reflex tachycardia worsens the shear force.
buzz: Blood pressure differential between arms with tearing pain radiating to the back.

pearl: NSAIDs plus colchicine, and colchicine is the part that cuts recurrence. Diffuse ST elevation with PR depression, unlike the territorial pattern of infarction.
buzz: Steroids increase recurrence. Avoid them unless the underlying cause demands it.

pearl: Only three interventions lower mortality: smoking cessation, long-term oxygen when PaO2 is 55 or less, and lung volume reduction in selected patients. Bronchodilators treat symptoms only.
buzz: Target saturation 88 to 92 percent. Chasing a normal number risks CO2 retention.

pearl: Step therapy by level of control, not by severity at diagnosis. ICS-formoterol is now preferred over a short-acting beta agonist alone, even for intermittent symptoms.
buzz: A normal or rising PaCO2 during an acute attack signals fatigue and impending respiratory failure, not improvement.

pearl: CURB-65 or PSI decides inpatient versus outpatient, and that disposition question is the testable part far more often than the diagnosis.
buzz: Cavitary upper-lobe infiltrate with foul sputum after an aspiration event points to anaerobes.

pearl: Light criteria separate exudate from transudate, and any single positive criterion makes it an exudate.
buzz: A parapneumonic effusion with pH under 7.2 needs a chest tube, not more antibiotics.

pearl: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis - needle decompression before any imaging. A small primary spontaneous pneumothorax can simply be observed on oxygen.
buzz: Tracheal deviation away from the affected side, absent breath sounds, hypotension. Do not wait for the film.

pearl: Bilateral hilar adenopathy with noncaseating granulomas. Treat only symptomatic or organ-threatening disease, since many cases remit spontaneously.
buzz: Hypercalcemia comes from macrophage 1-alpha-hydroxylase producing calcitriol, not from PTH.

pearl: Polysomnography diagnoses, CPAP treats. Untreated OSA is a leading driver of resistant hypertension and recurrent atrial fibrillation.
buzz: STOP-BANG screens. Resistant hypertension should always raise the question.

pearl: Low tidal volume at 6 mL/kg of PREDICTED body weight with plateau pressure under 30 is one of the few ventilator strategies proven to lower mortality.
buzz: Prone positioning for P/F ratio under 150. Predicted weight is calculated from height, never actual weight.

pearl: Airborne isolation immediately, three sputum AFB specimens, then RIPE for 2 months followed by rifampin and isoniazid for 4 more.
buzz: Isoniazid causes neuropathy, so give B6. Ethambutol causes optic neuritis. Rifampin turns secretions orange and induces P450.

pearl: Aggressive lactated Ringer solution, early enteral feeding rather than bowel rest, and analgesia. Antibiotics only for documented infected necrosis.
buzz: Gallstone pancreatitis with cholangitis needs ERCP. Otherwise cholecystectomy during the same admission to prevent recurrence.

pearl: Ultrasound first. Cholecystectomy within 72 hours beats delayed surgery on both complications and length of stay.
buzz: Fever, jaundice, and RUQ pain together (Charcot triad) is cholangitis, not cholecystitis - that needs biliary drainage.

pearl: Duodenal pain improves with food while gastric pain worsens with it. Test and treat H. pylori, then confirm eradication with urea breath test or stool antigen.
buzz: Serology stays positive after cure, so it can never confirm eradication. Recurrent refractory ulcers with diarrhea suggest gastrinoma.

pearl: Empiric PPI trial. Endoscopy is reserved for alarm features: dysphagia, weight loss, anemia, bleeding, or new onset at an older age.
buzz: Barrett esophagus is intestinal metaplasia on biopsy and earns surveillance endoscopy.

pearl: Continuous mucosal inflammation extending proximally from the rectum. Colonoscopic surveillance begins 8 years after diagnosis because of cancer risk.
buzz: Primary sclerosing cholangitis is the classic association, and it pushes colorectal cancer risk higher still, moving surveillance to the time of diagnosis.

pearl: Skip lesions with transmural inflammation, anywhere from mouth to anus. Smoking worsens Crohn while it paradoxically protects in ulcerative colitis.
buzz: Before starting an anti-TNF agent for fistulizing disease, screen for latent TB and hepatitis B.

pearl: Two standing surveillance obligations: endoscopy for varices, and ultrasound every 6 months for hepatocellular carcinoma.
buzz: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis is an ascitic PMN count of 250 or more. Cefotaxime plus albumin, because albumin reduces renal failure and mortality.

pearl: Lactulose first line with rifaximin added for recurrence. The real work is finding the precipitant: GI bleed, infection, constipation, dehydration.
buzz: Ammonia level does not correlate with severity and should not guide management.

pearl: CT diagnoses. Uncomplicated disease can be managed as an outpatient, and selected low-risk cases need no antibiotics at all.
buzz: Colonoscopy 6 to 8 weeks AFTER resolution to exclude malignancy, never during the acute episode given perforation risk.

pearl: CT in adults, ultrasound first in children and pregnancy. A classic presentation with peritonitis goes to the operating room without waiting on imaging.
buzz: Pain migrating from periumbilical to right lower quadrant reflects the shift from visceral to parietal peritoneal irritation.

pearl: Tissue transglutaminase IgA WITH a total IgA level, drawn while the patient is still eating gluten. Confirm with duodenal biopsy.
buzz: Dermatitis herpetiformis is essentially pathognomonic. Selective IgA deficiency causes false negative serology.

pearl: Over 3.5 g per day of proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia. The hypercoagulability comes from urinary antithrombin III loss.
buzz: Membranous nephropathy - check anti-PLA2R and screen for occult solid tumor in older adults.

pearl: Hematuria with RBC casts, hypertension, and oliguria. Complement level narrows the differential quickly: low in post-streptococcal GN, lupus, and MPGN.
buzz: Post-streptococcal GN has a low C3 that normalizes by 8 weeks. If it stays low, reconsider the diagnosis.

pearl: Separate prerenal (FENa under 1 percent, BUN to creatinine over 20) from ATN (FENa over 2 percent, muddy brown granular casts). That distinction drives fluids versus supportive care.
buzz: Dialyze for AEIOU: Acidosis, Electrolytes, Intoxication, Overload, Uremia with pericarditis or encephalopathy.

pearl: ACE inhibitors or ARBs slow progression when proteinuria is present, and SGLT2 inhibitors now do the same independent of diabetes.
buzz: A creatinine rise of up to 30 percent after starting an ACE inhibitor is expected. Continue the drug and recheck.

pearl: Calcium gluconate first to stabilize the myocardium, then insulin with glucose to shift potassium intracellularly, and only then something that actually removes it.
buzz: Peaked T waves, then widened QRS, then sine wave. Treat the ECG, not the number.

pearl: Correct no faster than 8 mEq/L per 24 hours to avoid osmotic demyelination. Severe neurologic symptoms justify hypertonic saline.
buzz: Assess volume status first. SIADH is euvolemic with concentrated urine and a low serum uric acid.

pearl: Noncontrast CT is the study. Stones under 5 mm usually pass spontaneously, and tamsulosin helps the 5 to 10 mm range.
buzz: Fever with an obstructing stone is a urologic emergency. Decompress, because antibiotics cannot sterilize an obstructed system.

pearl: Uncomplicated cystitis: nitrofurantoin, TMP-SMX, or fosfomycin. Do not treat asymptomatic bacteriuria except in pregnancy or before urologic instrumentation.
buzz: In pregnancy, avoid nitrofurantoin near term and TMP-SMX in the first trimester.

pearl: CK more than five times normal, treated with aggressive IV fluids to prevent pigment nephropathy. Urine dipstick is positive for blood with no RBCs on microscopy.
buzz: Expect hyperkalemia and hypocalcemia. Do not replace calcium unless symptomatic, since it redeposits during recovery.

pearl: Fluids first, then an insulin infusion. Add dextrose once glucose falls below 200 and keep insulin running until the anion gap closes.
buzz: The gap, not the glucose, is the endpoint. Overlap subcutaneous insulin by 1 to 2 hours before stopping the drip or the gap reopens.

pearl: Glucose often over 600 with osmolality above 320 and minimal ketosis. The free water deficit is substantially larger than in DKA.
buzz: Mental status tracks osmolality, not the glucose number.

pearl: TSH is the screening test. Start levothyroxine and recheck TSH in 6 weeks, since anything sooner is uninterpretable.
buzz: Start low in the elderly or with coronary disease. Pregnancy needs roughly a 30 percent dose increase immediately on confirmation.

pearl: Low TSH with high free T4. Radioactive iodine uptake distinguishes Graves disease (diffuse uptake) from thyroiditis (low uptake), which changes treatment entirely.
buzz: Beta blocker for symptoms. Methimazole is preferred except in the first trimester, where PTU is used.

pearl: Confirm cortisol excess first with 24-hour urine free cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol, or low-dose dexamethasone. Only then localize with ACTH.
buzz: Exogenous glucocorticoids are the most common cause overall - check the medication list before ordering anything.

pearl: Hypotension with hyponatremia and hyperkalemia. In crisis, give hydrocortisone before the cosyntropin stimulation result returns.
buzz: Dexamethasone does not cross-react with the cortisol assay, so you can treat first and test after.

pearl: High calcium with a high or inappropriately normal PTH. It is the most common cause of hypercalcemia in outpatients.
buzz: In inpatients, malignancy is more common - usually PTHrP mediated, with a SUPPRESSED PTH.

pearl: Beta blocker, then a thionamide, then iodine at least an hour later, plus glucocorticoids.
buzz: Order matters: iodine given before the thionamide supplies substrate and fuels hormone synthesis.

pearl: Microcytic with low ferritin and high TIBC. In men and postmenopausal women, assume GI blood loss until proven otherwise.
buzz: Ferritin is an acute phase reactant and can be falsely normal with inflammation. Check transferrin saturation.

pearl: Hydroxyurea reduces both crises and mortality. A vaso-occlusive crisis needs hydration and opioids, and transfusion is not the default.
buzz: Acute chest syndrome calls for exchange transfusion. Functional asplenia means encapsulated organisms and lifelong vaccination.

pearl: Isolated thrombocytopenia with an otherwise normal count and smear. It remains a diagnosis of exclusion.
buzz: Treat only for bleeding or platelets under 30k, with steroids or IVIG. Platelet transfusion only for life-threatening hemorrhage.

pearl: Low platelets AND low fibrinogen with prolonged PT and PTT and a high D-dimer. Treatment is directed entirely at the underlying cause.
buzz: The coagulation studies separate it from TTP, where PT and PTT are normal.

pearl: CRAB defines end-organ damage: hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, bone lesions. Use a skeletal survey or whole-body imaging.
buzz: A bone scan misses myeloma entirely, because the lesions are purely lytic with no osteoblastic reaction.

pearl: Often an incidental lymphocytosis with smudge cells on the smear. Early treatment does not improve survival, so observe until symptomatic.
buzz: Watch for autoimmune hemolytic anemia and for Richter transformation into aggressive lymphoma.

pearl: Reed-Sternberg cells with orderly contiguous nodal spread and a bimodal age distribution. Highly curable even at advanced stage.
buzz: B symptoms plus the classic alcohol-induced nodal pain.

pearl: Do not wait for the full pentad. Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia plus thrombocytopenia is enough to start plasma exchange urgently.
buzz: Platelet transfusion is contraindicated - it feeds ongoing microvascular thrombosis. ADAMTS13 deficiency is the mechanism.

pearl: Cultures then broad-spectrum antibiotics within the first hour, with 30 mL/kg of crystalloid for hypotension or lactate of 4 or more.
buzz: Norepinephrine is the first-line vasopressor. Antibiotic timing is the single strongest mortality lever.

pearl: With focal deficit, papilledema, seizure, or immunocompromise, give antibiotics and dexamethasone BEFORE the CT and lumbar puncture.
buzz: Never delay antibiotics for imaging. Dexamethasone with or before the first dose reduces hearing loss in pneumococcal disease.

pearl: Nonpurulent cellulitis needs streptococcal coverage such as cephalexin. Purulent disease needs drainage plus MRSA coverage.
buzz: Pain out of proportion to exam with rapid progression or crepitus means necrotizing fasciitis - a surgical emergency, not an antibiotic problem.

pearl: Oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin is first line. Metronidazole is no longer preferred except when nothing else is available.
buzz: Never test for cure - the assay stays positive. Multiply recurrent disease is an indication for fecal microbiota transplant.

pearl: MRI is the most sensitive imaging, and bone biopsy gives the organism that actually guides therapy. Plain films lag about 2 weeks behind.
buzz: In the diabetic foot, a positive probe-to-bone test substantially raises the likelihood.

pearl: EBV with a positive heterophile antibody. Avoid contact sports for 3 to 4 weeks because of splenic rupture risk.
buzz: Amoxicillin produces a morbilliform rash in mono - this is not a penicillin allergy.

pearl: Start antiretroviral therapy at diagnosis regardless of CD4 count. PCP prophylaxis at CD4 under 200, MAC prophylaxis under 50.
buzz: New diagnosis with meningitis: send cryptococcal antigen and measure opening pressure, since serial LPs for pressure control save lives.

pearl: Noncontrast CT to exclude hemorrhage, then tPA within 4.5 hours. Thrombectomy extends to 24 hours in selected large-vessel occlusions.
buzz: Do not lower blood pressure aggressively unless above 220/120, or above 185/110 when giving thrombolytics.

pearl: The deficit resolves completely, but stroke risk is highest in the first 48 hours - this is an urgent workup, not a reassuring event.
buzz: Symptomatic carotid stenosis of 70 to 99 percent warrants endarterectomy within 2 weeks.

pearl: A first unprovoked seizure with normal workup usually does not need a drug. In status, benzodiazepine first, then levetiracetam or fosphenytoin.
buzz: Check glucose and sodium immediately - reversible metabolic causes are the ones you must not miss.

pearl: Lesions disseminated in both time and space, supported by MRI and oligoclonal bands. Acute flares get high-dose steroids.
buzz: Heat transiently worsens existing symptoms (Uhthoff phenomenon) - this is not a true relapse and needs no treatment change.

pearl: Ascending weakness with areflexia and albuminocytologic dissociation on LP. IVIG or plasmapheresis - steroids do NOT help.
buzz: Serial forced vital capacity and negative inspiratory force decide intubation. Oxygen saturation stays normal until the patient crashes.

pearl: Bradykinesia plus resting tremor or rigidity. Carbidopa-levodopa is most effective; dopamine agonists are considered in younger patients to delay dyskinesia.
buzz: Early falls with vertical gaze palsy points to progressive supranuclear palsy instead.

pearl: Triptans for acute attacks. Add prophylaxis at 4 or more headache days per month: propranolol, topiramate, amitriptyline, or a CGRP agent.
buzz: Avoid triptans with uncontrolled hypertension or coronary disease. Medication overuse headache is the common trap.

pearl: Thunderclap worst headache of life. Noncontrast CT first, and if negative with persistent suspicion, lumbar puncture for xanthochromia.
buzz: Nimodipine reduces delayed cerebral ischemia from vasospasm - it improves outcome without much changing the vasospasm itself.

pearl: Fatigable weakness with ptosis and diplopia, worse through the day. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies plus chest CT for thymoma.
buzz: In crisis, follow FVC. Avoid aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, and magnesium, all of which worsen transmission.

pearl: Peripheral CN VII palsy that INVOLVES the forehead. Steroids within 72 hours plus eye protection to prevent exposure keratopathy.
buzz: Forehead sparing means a central lesion - that patient needs brain imaging, not prednisone.

pearl: Acute, fluctuating inattention with an underlying medical cause. The job is finding the cause; nonpharmacologic measures come first.
buzz: Antipsychotics only for dangerous agitation. Benzodiazepines worsen delirium except when it is alcohol withdrawal.

pearl: Insidious memory loss with preserved alertness. Cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are modestly symptomatic and do not alter course.
buzz: Gait disturbance and urinary incontinence appearing EARLY alongside cognitive decline suggests normal pressure hydrocephalus.

pearl: Symmetric small joint pain with morning stiffness over an hour. Start a DMARD such as methotrexate early - the window for preventing erosion is short.
buzz: Anti-CCP is far more specific than rheumatoid factor. Screen for latent TB before any anti-TNF agent.

pearl: ANA is sensitive; anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith are specific. Hydroxychloroquine is indicated for essentially every patient.
buzz: Falling complement with rising dsDNA suggests active nephritis - that is a biopsy, not a dose adjustment.

pearl: Negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals. Treat the flare with NSAIDs, colchicine, or steroids - urate level is irrelevant acutely.
buzz: Do not start OR stop urate-lowering therapy during a flare, but continue it if the patient is already established on it.

pearl: Start high-dose steroids the moment you suspect it. Temporal artery biopsy stays positive for up to 2 weeks, so treatment never waits on tissue.
buzz: Vision loss is irreversible and often the presenting event. Jaw claudication is the most specific symptom.

pearl: Mechanical pain worse with use, with stiffness under 30 minutes. Exercise and weight loss outperform most pharmacology.
buzz: No systemic inflammation - ESR and CRP are normal, which is the fastest separation from inflammatory arthritis.

pearl: Proximal girdle pain and stiffness with a high ESR, and a dramatic response to low-dose steroids that is nearly diagnostic.
buzz: Ask about jaw claudication and visual symptoms at every visit, because giant cell arteritis overlaps in a substantial minority.

pearl: Inflammatory back pain that IMPROVES with exercise and worsens with rest, with sacroiliitis on imaging and HLA-B27 association.
buzz: Screen for anterior uveitis. NSAIDs first, anti-TNF if refractory.

pearl: New hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or end-organ features. Magnesium for seizure prophylaxis; delivery is the only cure.
buzz: Magnesium toxicity goes reflexes first, then respiration. Calcium gluconate is the antidote.

pearl: Beta-hCG above the discriminatory zone with no intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound. Methotrexate if stable and criteria are met.
buzz: Methotrexate is contraindicated with fetal cardiac activity, mass over 3.5 cm, or very high hCG. Unstable means surgery.

pearl: PAINFUL bleeding with a firm tender uterus. This is a clinical diagnosis - ultrasound is frequently normal and cannot exclude it.
buzz: Cocaine use, trauma, and hypertension are the classic precipitants.

pearl: PAINLESS bright red bleeding in the third trimester. Never perform a digital exam until ultrasound has located the placenta.
buzz: Delivery is by cesarean. A prior cesarean substantially raises the risk of placenta accreta.

pearl: Rotterdam criteria need two of three: oligo-ovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries. Screen for diabetes and dyslipidemia.
buzz: Unopposed estrogen drives endometrial hyperplasia. A progestin or combined OCP protects the endometrium even when fertility is not the goal.

pearl: Cyclic pelvic pain with dyspareunia and infertility. Laparoscopy is definitive, but empiric treatment comes first.
buzz: NSAIDs and combined OCPs first line, GnRH agonists second. Severity of disease correlates poorly with severity of pain.

pearl: Screen at 24 to 28 weeks. Diet and exercise first, then insulin, which does not cross the placenta.
buzz: Retest with a 75 g OGTT at 6 to 12 weeks postpartum - lifetime type 2 diabetes risk is high.

pearl: Fever 5 days or more plus four of five: conjunctivitis, rash, cervical adenopathy, oral changes, extremity changes. IVIG plus aspirin.
buzz: Echocardiography for coronary aneurysms. This is the one setting where children are given aspirin.

pearl: Barky cough with inspiratory stridor and a steeple sign. A single dose of dexamethasone for everyone, and nebulized epinephrine if there is stridor at rest.
buzz: Drooling, toxic appearance, and tripoding points to epiglottitis instead - do not examine the throat.

pearl: RSV in infants, managed with supportive care alone. Bronchodilators, steroids, and antibiotics have all failed to show benefit.
buzz: Apnea can be the presenting sign in young infants, before any respiratory distress is obvious.

pearl: Colicky pain with legs drawn up, currant jelly stool, and a sausage-shaped mass. Ultrasound shows the target sign.
buzz: Air or contrast enema is both diagnostic and therapeutic - it is the treatment, not just the test.

pearl: Nonbilious projectile vomiting at 3 to 6 weeks with hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.
buzz: Correct the electrolytes BEFORE surgery. This is a medical emergency and a surgical elective.

pearl: Simple febrile seizure is generalized, under 15 minutes, once in 24 hours, between 6 months and 5 years. No EEG, no imaging, no LP by default.
buzz: Do not start antiepileptics. Antipyretics are for comfort and do not prevent recurrence.

pearl: SSRIs first line. Assess response at 4 to 6 weeks, and continue 6 to 12 months after remission to prevent relapse.
buzz: Always screen for a history of mania before starting an antidepressant.

pearl: Lithium is the agent with evidence for reducing suicide. Check thyroid and renal function before starting and periodically after.
buzz: Antidepressant monotherapy can precipitate mania - it must be paired with a mood stabilizer.

pearl: Six months or more of symptoms including a month of active phase. Clozapine is reserved for treatment-resistant disease and is the most effective agent.
buzz: Clozapine requires ANC monitoring for agranulocytosis, and also causes myocarditis, seizures, and severe constipation.

pearl: Excessive worry most days for 6 months or more. SSRI or SNRI combined with cognitive behavioral therapy.
buzz: Benzodiazepines only as a short bridge - dependence, falls, and cognitive effects outweigh the benefit long term.

pearl: Restriction with low body weight and body image disturbance. Weight restoration is the first priority and precedes psychotherapy gains.
buzz: Refeeding syndrome: watch phosphate, magnesium, and potassium. Start low and advance slowly.

pearl: Symptoms persisting beyond 1 month after trauma. Trauma-focused CBT is first line, with SSRIs also effective.
buzz: Prazosin targets nightmares. Benzodiazepines worsen outcomes and should be avoided.

pearl: Mucosal involvement with epidermal detachment under 10 percent BSA; over 30 percent is toxic epidermal necrolysis. Stop the offending drug immediately.
buzz: Sulfonamides, allopurinol, anticonvulsants, and NSAIDs are the classic culprits. Manage like a burn, with fluid and wound care.

pearl: Well-demarcated plaques with silvery scale on extensor surfaces. Topical steroids plus vitamin D analogs for limited disease.
buzz: Screen for psoriatic arthritis and metabolic syndrome - the comorbidities are the tested part.

pearl: ABCDE for recognition, then EXCISIONAL biopsy with narrow margins. Breslow depth drives both prognosis and definitive margins.
buzz: Never shave-biopsy a suspected melanoma - it destroys the depth measurement that staging depends on.

pearl: Intramuscular epinephrine into the anterolateral thigh immediately, repeated as needed. There is no dose ceiling and no absolute contraindication.
buzz: Antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts that never replace epinephrine. Observe for a biphasic reaction hours later.

pearl: IV saline for volume first, calcitonin for speed, and a bisphosphonate for durable control. PTH is suppressed, unlike primary hyperparathyroidism.
buzz: Loop diuretics are old teaching and worsen dehydration - use them only once the patient is volume overloaded.

pearl: Clonus, hyperreflexia, agitation, and autonomic instability appearing within HOURS of a serotonergic drug or interaction.
buzz: Hyperreflexia and clonus separate it from neuroleptic malignant syndrome, which has lead-pipe rigidity and evolves over days.

pearl: Fever, lead-pipe rigidity, altered mental status, and a high CK after antipsychotic exposure. Stop the drug; dantrolene or bromocriptine for severe cases.
buzz: Onset over days to weeks, versus hours for serotonin syndrome. Rigidity is lead-pipe, not clonic.

pearl: Confusion, ophthalmoplegia, and ataxia from thiamine deficiency. Give thiamine BEFORE glucose in anyone with alcohol use disorder.
buzz: Glucose administered first consumes remaining thiamine and can precipitate or worsen the encephalopathy.

pearl: Betamethasone from 24 to 34 weeks for fetal lung maturity, and magnesium under 32 weeks for neuroprotection.
buzz: Tocolysis buys 48 hours to complete steroids. It does not meaningfully prolong pregnancy and is not the goal.

pearl: Plot total bilirubin on the hour-specific nomogram - the absolute number alone means nothing without age in hours. Phototherapy by threshold.
buzz: Jaundice within the first 24 hours of life is always pathologic. Think hemolysis, and check blood type and Coombs.

pearl: Sawtooth flutter waves, commonly 2 to 1 conduction giving a ventricular rate near 150. Anticoagulation follows the same rules as atrial fibrillation.
buzz: Cavotricuspid isthmus ablation is highly curative, considerably more so than ablation for atrial fibrillation.
